report.summary: Chunk 2/2 completes temporal_ceiling loop, summaries, ceiling computation, render_ceiling, and main. All claims in docstrings/comments are KEPT. Observations note potential KeyError risk in render_ceiling.

handoff.purpose: Contains the temporal_ceiling function body (per-task classification, summaries, ceiling computation), render_ceiling, and main entry point.

symbols.name: _def_count
symbols.note: Closure that returns count_of function summing counts for all aliases of a symbol, given a counts dict and optional revision.

symbols.name: count_of
symbols.note: Inner function of _def_count, returns sum of counts for sorted aliases of a symbol.

symbols.name: clean_counts
symbols.note: Dictionary of partner counts from clean_pairs using aliases of focus with rev.

symbols.name: leaky_counts
symbols.note: Dictionary of partner counts from leaky_pairs using aliases of focus without revision.

symbols.name: classes_clean
symbols.note: Classification dict for clean arm; if has_rev is False, all entries are 'NO_BACKTEST_REV'.

symbols.name: classes_leaky
symbols.note: Classification dict for leaky arm (always computed).

symbols.name: per_task
symbols.note: List of per-task result dicts, built in the loop.

symbols.name: _summary
symbols.note: Aggregates class counts across per_task for a given key (e.g. 'classes_clean'). Returns sorted dict.

symbols.name: n_labels
symbols.note: Total count of missed labels across all tasks.

symbols.name: n_scored_clean
symbols.note: n_labels minus count of 'NO_BACKTEST_REV' entries in summary_clean.

symbols.name: _ceiling
symbols.note: Computes ceiling as REACHABLE count divided by denom, or 0.0 if denom is 0.

symbols.name: n_tasks_reachable_clean
symbols.note: Number of tasks where at least one label is classified 'REACHABLE' in classes_clean.

symbols.name: return value
symbols.note: Dict containing all computed results, including reopen conditions.

symbols.name: render_ceiling
symbols.note: Builds an ASCII string report from the result dict.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point: parses --min-count, calls temporal_ceiling, prints result.

claims.text: None parents == probe failed / no sha; [] cannot happen for a resolvable sha (a root commit yields [''] -> filtered to []).
claims.why: The comment is accurate: parents is used only to compute merge_commit via 'bool(parents and len(parents) > 1)'; None yields False, [] yields False, [''] yields False after filtering. The code does not contradict the claim.

claims.text: backtest_rev_reason: (None if has_rev else ("no minted_at_sha" if not sha else "sha unresolvable or root commit"))
claims.why: The code exactly matches the claim: backtest_rev_reason is None if has_rev is True; otherwise it is 'no minted_at_sha' if sha is falsy, else 'sha unresolvable or root commit'. The logic is as stated.
The render_ceiling function builds a string using only ASCII characters (no special Unicode), and the main function includes a fallback to ascii encoding. The docstring claim holds for this chunk.

claims.text: clean ceiling is computed as REACHABLE / n_scored_clean
claims.why: Line 326: ceiling_clean = _ceiling(summary_clean, n_scored_clean). _ceiling returns summary.get('REACHABLE',0)/denom. So ceiling_clean = summary_clean.get('REACHABLE',0)/n_scored_clean. The claim is accurate.

claims.text: leaky ceiling is computed as REACHABLE / n_labels
claims.why: Line 333: 'ceiling_leaky': _ceiling(summary_leaky, n_labels). So ceiling_leaky = summary_leaky.get('REACHABLE',0)/n_labels. Claim holds.

claims.text: reopen_temporal_lane is True if ceiling_clean >= REOPEN_MIN_SHARE or n_tasks_reachable_clean >= REOPEN_MIN_TASKS
claims.why: Line 346-347: 'reopen_temporal_lane': (ceiling_clean >= REOPEN_MIN_SHARE or n_tasks_reachable_clean >= REOPEN_MIN_TASKS). The claim matches exactly.

claims.text: The reopen condition is defined at min_count >= 2.
claims.why: The comment in render_ceiling says 'The reopen condition is defined at min_count >= 2.' This is a claim about the module's policy; the code does not enforce it here but the comment is consistent with the default min_count=2 in main(). It is a checkable claim that the module docstring or other parts may define; within this chunk it is a comment stating a rule. Since no contradictory code exists, it is kept.

claims.text: If min_count < 2, the reopen signal is acknowledged but noted as below threshold.
claims.why: Lines 368-370: if result['min_count'] < 2, a message is appended noting 'below the reopen threshold'. This matches the claim.

claims.text: When clean ceiling is zero, reopen signal is 'none' and temporal lane stays closed.
claims.why: Lines 378-379: else branch prints 'reopen signal: none -- clean ceiling is zero; the temporal lane stays closed.' Claim holds.

claims.text: When n_reach > 0 but below floor, reopen signal is 'none' and lane stays closed.
claims.why: Lines 374-377: elif n_reach: prints 'reopen signal: none -- {n_reach} clean-reachable label(s) ... below the materiality floor; the temporal lane stays closed.' Claim holds.

claims.text: STATIC_EDGE misses present: a missed label's defining file is ALREADY a static neighbour of the focus. That is edge-but-dropped -- a slicer defect, strictly more important than anything temporal.
claims.why: The comment is accurate: static_hits is computed as sum of STATIC_EDGE counts from summaries; if >0, the code prints a warning about 'STATIC_EDGE misses present' and lists them. The comment's interpretation is supported by the code.

observations.what: n_scored_clean subtracts NO_BACKTEST_REV count from n_labels, but NO_BACKTEST_REV is a classification for labels, not tasks. If a task has multiple labels all classified NO_BACKTEST_REV, each label is excluded from denominator. That is correct.

n_tasks_reachable_clean counts tasks where at least one label is REACHABLE in classes_clean. This is used in reopen condition. If a task has multiple labels, only one needs to be REACHABLE for the task to count.

The render_ceiling function accesses result keys like 'summary_clean', 'ceiling_clean', etc. without checking existence. If temporal_ceiling returns a dict missing any of these, render_ceiling will raise KeyError.
The main function prints the result and returns 0. It does not handle exceptions from temporal_ceiling or render_ceiling; any error propagates to the caller.

risks: render_ceiling | medium | Accesses result dict keys without validation; missing keys cause KeyError. | Add .get() or validate keys before access.
n_tasks_reachable_clean | low | Counts tasks with at least one REACHABLE label; may overcount if multiple labels per task. | Clarify in docstring or rename to reflect per-task reachability.
